description.narrative:
The proposal is an outcome of the gap assessment carried out by national experts, and approved by the ministry of Environment, supported through the Swedish funded SANE27 program. The gap assessment has covered all Technical Assistance needs for transposition of legislation, capacity building and implementation in order to have successful negotations and reach EU-standards. Work on the gap assessment has involved a number of government officials within the Ministry of Tourism and Environment (MTE), Ministry of Infrastructure and Energy (MIE), State Inspectorate on Environment, Forests, Water and Tourism, National Environmental Agency (NEA) and also representatives from civil society.
The Project costs are 10.7 MSEK and the expected main project results are: R1. The national and local authorities have a model for waste separation at source; R2. Providing technical assistance to the national and local authorities (waste sector within ministry and Berat local authorities) to develop their capacities in the management of the scheme. R3. Introduction of a public communications campaign to support the new waste scheme; R4. Introduction and procurement of the basic infrastructure required for source separation in Berat municipality sustainable in the Albanian local context.
Sida will enter into a grant agreement with MTE, the Ministry being the policy maker for solid waste and the coordinator of the preparations for EU negotiations. A MoU between Sida and Berat Municipality will be established. The embassy will procure the support of an international Consultant and will manage the contract and financial management of funds. The reason for this is based on the need to address different risk factors, e g the lack of government capacity to carry out the procurement which risks delaying the start of the contribution as well as corruption risks.

title.narrative: Amendment No 2 to the Agreement between the Swedish Development Cooperation Agency Sida and the Ministry of Tourism and Environment of the Republic of Albania on a household source separation project in Berat municipality
Amendment of contribution Household Source Separation National Model
Decision household source separation, national model

description.narrative:
Operational municipal sourceseparation system established: The project successfully established and operationalised Albania's first municipal household sourceseparation service aligned with EU standards. Central to this achievement was the creation and strengthening of Berat City Green, a public joint stock company wholly owned by Berat Municipality, which now manages the service. Through extensive capacity building and on the job mentoring, municipal staff and company personnel developed the technical and operational skills required to run the system effectively. The project also financed and installed the necessary infrastructure and equipment, including collection bins, bags, vehicles, a sorting station and associated machinery, while a large scale public awareness campaign, including door to door outreach, promoted citizen participation. The resulting model has strengthened municipal oversight of waste management, enabled service improvements based on user feedback, and created a mechanism through which revenues from recyclable materials can be reinvested directly into further service development.
Increased recovery of recyclable materials: Households are now separating and contributing approximately 15 tonnes of recyclable materials per month, creating a steady stream of materials ready for sale and recycling.
Reduced greenhouse gas emissions: According to the consultants calculations, between January and August 2025, the source separation system in Berat generated estimated climate benefits of 109,368 kg CO2 avoided emissions. These savings resulted from both the recycling of cardboard, which is significantly more resource efficient than producing virgin materials, and the diversion of recyclable waste from landfill, reducing carbon dioxide and methane emissions.
Improved livelihoods for informal waste pickers: The project facilitated the formal employment of informal waste pickers, significantly improving their working conditions through regular salaries, safer work environments, and enhanced health and social protection benefits. These positive impacts were recognised in the EDEN Centre/Bankwatch reportwhere it is stated that the Municipality represents a rare example of how the integration of informal waste pickers into a newly operational recycling system can generate tangible results. It further states that municipal management expressed strong satisfaction with the skills, efficiency, and practical knowledge that these informal waste pickers contributed, especially at the sorting centre. Their expertise was widely recognised as an invaluable contribution to the overall professionalism of the scheme.
First municipal auction of recyclables in Albania: The project supported theorganisation of Albania's first municipal auction of recyclable materials. Through this process, 65 tonnes of cardboard were sold at 110 ALL/kg (approximately€115/tonne), a competitive outcome comparable to regional market conditions. The auction mechanism has since been institutionalised and continues to beused for the sale of cardboard and plastics, including after project completion.
Improved waste data and planning: Installation and operation of a weighbridge at the sorting station revealed that Berat was disposing of approximately 50% more waste than previously estimated. This has significantly improved the accuracy of municipal waste data and provides an important lesson for waste management planning and reporting across Albania.
